# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).
data.title: Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

# Coordination-mode batch continuation + deferred leadership hand-off

Parent AC4: on the production coordination path the leader must source continuation audit targets from its own Herdr head (bounded window extension, same ranking) without releasing leadership mid-batch, and defer the own-backlog leadership hand-off until the batch ends.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Covers parent AC2: Sequential single-audit safety: every continuation re-checks the idle-duration gate, `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2`, proxy contention, code freeze, the active-audit markers and single-flight — no gate is relaxed, only the post-dispatch idle reset is deferred.
- Covers parent AC3: No duplicate or re-dispatched items: each continuation selects a distinct item through the existing classification and dispatched-marker exclusions, and any non-`dispatched` outcome ends the batch.
- Covers parent AC4: Coordination-mode compatibility: the leader sources continuation targets from its own Herdr head without releasing leadership mid-batch, and hands off leadership once at batch end.

- **Continuation source (AC4).** After a successful batch-eligible audit dispatch, `dispatchFromCoordination` may dispatch the next audit target from the leader's own head extension (`getHerdrListHead` + `fetchExtendedHerdrItems`, `includeNonCritical` filter as today) instead of only after total offer-list exhaustion — still exactly one dispatch per invocation, never two.
- **Same filters (AC3/AC4).** Every own-head continuation passes the identical sequential filters as the existing own-backlog fallback: `classifyItemForDispatch`, dispatched-marker exclusion (id-guard + staleness), attempt budget, non-terminal cooldown, code-freeze, audit slot minimum (≥2), in-flight critical guard, review-queue hold for implements. The continuation selects only `audit`-kind items.
- **No duplicate target (AC3).** The item just dispatched, and any item already dispatched in this batch, is never re-selected in the same batch — enforced by the existing marker exclusion plus an explicit batch-local exclusion set, covered by a test.
- **Leadership timing (AC4).** An own-backlog (`ownBacklogDispatch === true`) audit dispatch during an active batch with budget remaining does NOT trigger `releaseLeadership()` in that tick; the step-down happens exactly once at batch end (cap reached, depth dropped, failed continuation, or the next tick when the batch is no longer active). A normal in-view dispatch is unchanged.
- **No regression.** Non-batch coordination dispatch, leader election/lease TTL, coordination check-ins, pruning and the offer path are unchanged; `dispatchFromCoordination` direct-API callers without `freeSlots`/`auditBatchMax` keep today's behaviour (fail-open).

## Minimal Implementation

- Thread `auditBatchMax` and the batch-continuation intent through `dispatchFromCoordination`'s options (a boolean/marker set by `tick()` when the batch is active, plus the dispatched-target set for the current batch).
- Factor the existing own-backlog candidate loop into a reusable helper so the continuation path applies the exact same filters (no duplicated filter chain).
- Add `auditBatchContinuation?: boolean` (and any needed batch metadata) to `DowntimeDispatchOutcome`, documented, so `tick()` can decide the leadership step-down and the idle-reset deferral without re-deriving state.
- In `tick()`, gate the existing `outcome.ownBacklogDispatch === true` step-down on batch-inactive (deferring it to batch end).
- Cover with the coordination-dispatch and orchestrator specs from C1.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts
- packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts

## Dependencies

- Depends on the depth/reset item (C3) for the batch state and outcome surface.
- Depends on the observability item (C5) for the continuation token contract.

## Deliverables

- Leader own-head continuation with unchanged filter semantics and deferred step-down, with green coordination-dispatch/orchestrator tests.
data.title: Coordination batch continuation + deferred leadership hand-off

# Observability: audit-batch decision tokens and metadata

Parent AC5: every batch decision is recorded in the existing downtime decision log at the existing rate limit. Existing reason tokens are unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Covers parent AC5: Observability: every batch decision is recorded in the downtime decision log with a distinct reason token (`audit-batch-continue` and the existing held/blocked tokens) including depth, cap and remaining; rate limiting is unchanged.

- **Continuation token (AC5).** An accepted audit-batch continuation records a distinct token (e.g. `audit-batch-continue`) in the existing decision log with metadata: `depth`, `cap`, `remaining`, plus today's standard fields (`freeSlots`, `totalSlots`, `ownerPresent`, `runningPanes`, `contentionDepth`).
- **Blocked continuation tokens (AC5).** Held/blocked continuations reuse the existing tokens unchanged — `audit-in-flight` (per-worklog single-flight) and `audit-host-saturated` (host-wide marker) for marker blocks, `slot-owned`, `proxy-contention`, `code-freeze`, `review-queue-hold`, `no-candidate` — with the batch metadata (depth/cap/remaining) attached when a batch was active.
- **Batch end observability.** Batch deactivation transitions that would otherwise be silent surface in the decision log where a distinct signal adds value (e.g. cap reached / depth dropped) without spamming the log — still rate-limited by `DOWNTIME_DECISION_LOG_MIN_INTERVAL_MS`.
- **Rate limiting + header unchanged.** The header blocking token updates on every refusal exactly as today; `DOWNTIME_DECISION_LOG_MIN_INTERVAL_MS` behaviour is preserved for refusals; no existing reason-token test regresses.
- **Doc alignment.** The new/attached tokens match the token list committed in the docs item (C6).

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend the decision-log entry shape (`CoordinationLogEntry` kind `decision`) with optional `batch?: { depth: number; cap: number; remaining: number }` + the `audit-batch-continue`/`audit-batch-held`(if distinct signal) reasons routed through the worker's `recordDecision`.
- Emit the continuation token from `tick()` after a batch-armed continuation attempt (accepted or held) with the live depth/cap/remaining; re-compute depth from the head the same way as C3.
- Update the reason-token comment blocks in `downtime-worker.ts` and the dispatcher doc token list (§~60/108).
- Cover with the decision-log specs from C1 (`downtime-log.test.ts`).

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts
- docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md (token list)

## Dependencies

- Depends on the depth/reset item (C3) for the batch state and depth computation.

## Deliverables

- Observable batch decisions (token + depth/cap/remaining metadata) with green token/metadata specs.

All related documentation (incl. code comments) is updated and consistent with shipped behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Covers parent AC7: Documentation: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` and the settings reference document the new setting, the activation rule, the sequential safety invariants and the new decision tokens.

- **Dispatcher doc.** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` documents:

# F5 — Tests: lazy command registry, help and plugin fidelity

Test-first coverage for the lazy per-command registry (F6), including the parent AC5 graceful-degradation fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test asserts that a normal command (`wl show <id> --json`) does not import unrelated command modules (static assertion on the registry's dynamic-import map, or a module-load sentinel).
- `--help` and bare `wl` still list all built-in commands in the grouped layout with global options, compared against the current output (plugin entries excluded from the snapshot).
- Plugin registration still runs on the heavy path (`loadPlugins`) and plugin commands appear in help.
- Fallback (parent AC5): when registry resolution fails (missing module or rejecting import), the CLI falls back to eager full registration and the command still runs; covered by a fault-injection test that mocks a rejecting dynamic import.
- Unknown commands keep the current error and exit behaviour (snapshot).
- `tests/cli/completion.test.ts` and `tests/cli/smoke.test.ts` pass unchanged.
- Covers parent AC5: if lazy loading or the split entry point fails for any command, behaviour falls back to today's fully-registered CLI — no functional regression, help and plugin registration intact.


**Key Files:**

- `tests/cli/smoke.test.ts`

# F4 — Split the CLI entry: thin fast path, dynamically imported heavy graph

Implements desired change #1: `src/cli.ts` becomes a thin bootstrap (argv scan, read-cache fast path, `--version`) that dynamically imports the current heavy graph (`src/cli-main.ts`) only when a cache hit did not serve the invocation. This is the largest single lever for parent AC1.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/cli.ts` statically imports only the fast-path allowlist; `commander`, command modules, `plugin-loader`, `cli-utils`, `lib/runtime` and `better-sqlite3` load only through dynamic `import()` inside `cli-main.ts`.
- The F2 budget file is tightened in the same change: the recorded fast-path graph becomes the allowlist, so a future eager import fails the ratchet test.
- A served cache hit exits before any heavy module loads; `wl --version` prints the version from `src/version.ts` and exits without heavy imports.
- Every command behaves identically: full suite green, including `tests/cli/read-cache-e2e.test.ts` and `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` unchanged (parent AC4).
- Cache semantics untouched: cache key/argv extraction, TTL/LRU, WAL-aware invalidation, write-to-read freshness and byte-identical JSON (parent AC4).
- Worktree detection/process registration and the `--worklog-dir` override still run on whichever path executes; no regression for `wl` inside a worktree.
- The `/usr/local/bin/wl` → `dist/cli.js` contract is preserved; `npm run build` emits both `dist/cli.js` and `dist/cli-main.js`.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Move the current program construction, registration, help formatting, plugin loading and runtime initialisation into `src/cli-main.ts`, exporting an async `main(argv)`.
2. Keep argv normalisation, read-cache lookup, spawn recording and version printing in `src/cli.ts`; otherwise `await import('./cli-main.js')`.
3. Keep the write-invalidation hook on the shared path so writes still bump the state counter.

**Key Files:**
- `src/cli.ts`
- `src/cli-main.ts`
- `src/read-cache-cli.ts`
- `src/version.ts`
- `src/process-lifecycle.ts`
- `src/worklog-paths.ts`

## Dependencies

- F3 (tests first).
data.title: Split CLI entry: thin fast path, dynamic heavy graph

# F6 — Lazy per-command imports via a command registry

Implements desired change #2: replace the 35 eager `import XCommand` lines with a name → `() => import('./commands/x.js')` registry, resolved on demand. Only the command that actually runs loads its module; `--help` and bare `wl` may load all (rare).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/cli-main.ts` registers commands through the registry; no static imports of `./commands/*` remain.
- A single-command invocation loads only that command module (verified by F5's isolation test); `--help` and bare `wl` load all command modules and produce identical grouped help output.
- Plugin loading and `initializeRuntime` ordering is unchanged for commands that need them; commands that do not touch the DB still avoid opening it (visible in F1 spawn record kinds).
- Graceful degradation (parent AC5): a registry resolution error logs one warning, falls back to eager full registration, then dispatches the command; covered by F5's fault-injection test.
- Full suite green; existing read-cache, e2e and spawn-reduction suites unchanged (parent AC4).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Declare a registry mapping each name in the existing `builtInCommandNames` set to a dynamic import of its module.
2. Resolve the single command token from argv before `program.parse()` and register only that command (falling back to all for `--help`/bare invocation/unknown token).
3. Keep help grouping metadata independent of module loading.

**Key Files:**
- `src/cli-main.ts`
- `src/command-registry.ts`
- `src/commands/*.ts`
- `src/plugin-loader.ts`

## Dependencies

- F5 (tests first).

# F7 — Fast-path import slimming to the 0.5 s / 60 MB budget

Parent AC1 sets a deliberately tight budget: p95 <= 0.5 s wall and <= 60 MB peak RSS for warm cache hits, against a bare-node floor of 0.35 s / 58 MB and today's `read-cache-cli` graph at 0.46 s / 61 MB. After F4/F6 the fast path still imports the read-cache graph, so this item shaves it until the budget is met and then freezes the win.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Warm cache-hit `wl next --json`, `wl list --status open --json` and `wl --version` on the reference host: p95 wall <= 0.5 s and peak RSS <= 60 MB (F2 benchmark, >= 10 runs), with before and after numbers quoted in a comment.
- The fast-path graph no longer imports `commander`, `better-sqlite3`, `plugin-loader`, `cli-utils`, `lib/runtime`, `config` or schema/validation plumbing; the F2 ratchet is tightened and its budget updated to the parent AC1 target (p95 <= 0.5 s, peak RSS <= 60 MB).
- The specific reductions are recorded (for example: version read from `src/version.ts`, minimal worklog-dir resolution on the fast path, hashing/crypto deferred to the miss path, argv handling without `cli-utils`).
- No correctness change: cache keys, freshness and JSON bytes identical (parent AC4); full suite green.
- If the 60 MB target proves unreachable, the item records the measured floor with evidence and raises an OPEN QUESTION on the parent instead of silently relaxing the AC.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Re-run the F2 harness and profile the fast-path import graph.
2. Replace heavy imports still reachable from `read-cache-cli` (worklog-dir resolution, hashing, argv helpers) with minimal equivalents, deferring them to miss paths.
3. Tighten the F2 allowlist to the final set so the win cannot silently regress.

**Key Files:**
- `src/cli.ts`
- `src/read-cache-cli.ts`
- `src/read-cache.ts`
- `src/worklog-paths.ts`
- `tests/cli/startup-import-budget.test.ts`
- `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts`

## Dependencies

- F2 (harness and baseline)
- F4 (entry split)
- F6 (lazy registry, for the non-cache-hit command cost)
data.title: Fast-path import slimming to the 0.5 s / 60 MB budget

# F9 — Bound and prune the cache state directory via `wl doctor cache`

Implements desired change #4 and parent AC3: make the per-worklog-dir state counters a bounded, prunable on-disk store with a documented maintenance path, without touching freshness semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Opportunistic pruning on cache writes keeps `state/` at or under a configured bound (default file count around 1,000 plus a TTL for untouched counters, aligned with the existing entry TTL/LRU). Measured on the reference host: a pre-populated 200k-file `state/` is reduced to the bound by one prune run, with file count, inode count and bytes quoted before and after in a comment.
- `wl doctor cache` exists with `--json`, a dry-run (report-only) mode and a prune mode. It reports file count, total bytes, stale-by-TTL count and live-dir count, and reclaims space when pruning. Bare `wl doctor` mentions pending cache state.
- Pruning is atomic and concurrency-safe (temp+rename, never truncating a live counter mid-write) and never deletes a counter whose worklog dir still has fresh cache entries; if entries exist, they are invalidated before the counter is dropped.
- Freshness correctness intact: the read-cache suites pass unchanged (parent AC4) and no stale read is served because a counter was pruned.
- The cap is configurable (env var or config key) with defaults safe on a Raspberry Pi class host, and the default is documented.
- Covers parent AC3: `~/.cache/wl/state/` is bounded and prunable — state storage is capped or consolidated, stale entries are removed, and a documented maintenance path (`wl doctor cache` or automatic pruning) reclaims it, with freshness semantics unchanged.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add `pruneStateDir(cacheDir, { maxFiles, ttlMs, dryRun })` returning counts and bytes reclaimed.
2. Call it opportunistically and rate-limited (for example at most once per N minutes per process) from the cache write path, so growth is bounded without a daemon.
3. Add the `wl doctor cache` subcommand wiring the same function, reporting in text and `--json`.

**Key Files:**
- `src/read-cache.ts`
- `src/commands/doctor.ts`
- `src/read-cache-cli.ts`
- `CLI.md`
- `CONFIG.md`

## Dependencies

- F8 (tests first).
data.title: Bound and prune cache state via wl doctor cache

# F10 — Verify the >= 60 % CPU-second reduction per refresh cycle

Parent AC2's measurement and decision point. With F1 instrumentation, measure total CPU-seconds per 30 s refresh cycle across >= 4 panes on one shared worklog dir, before and after the fast path, and only then decide whether herdr read coalescing is additionally required.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A repeatable measurement procedure is recorded (env `WL_SPAWN_COUNT_FILE`, 4 panes running the herdr query set over one 30 s cycle, warm cache) with the exact command quoted in a comment.
- Baseline and after numbers are both quoted in comments on this item and on the parent: total CPU-seconds, spawn count, cache-hit count, p95 per-spawn wall time and RSS.
- After <= 0.4x baseline total CPU-seconds (>= 60 % reduction) is demonstrated, or the shortfall is quantified with the dominant remaining cost identified.
- If the target is missed, the item records which lever is needed. Given herdr already has in-flight memoisation and in-process SQLite reads (`WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG`, `WL-0MV6C6SLB005HX7B`), it either (a) implements a bounded, stateless coalescing refinement in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (one consolidated read per refresh tick) or (b) files a `discovered-from` child when the change exceeds this item's scope.
- No correctness regression: herdr refresh output is unchanged for the same DB state and the spawn-reduction simulation test still passes.
- Covers parent AC2: total CPU-seconds per 30 s refresh cycle across >= 4 panes on a shared worklog dir drops >= 60 % versus current behaviour, measured by the env-gated spawn instrumentation with per-process CPU time; baseline and after numbers quoted.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Build a 4-pane measurement harness reusing the patterns in `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` plus F1 aggregation.
2. Measure the pre-split build first (worktree of `dev`, or `WL_CACHE_DISABLED=1` for the read-work baseline), then re-measure after F4 to F7.
3. Record numbers and the lever decision in comments.

**Key Files:**
- `src/spawn-counter.ts`
- `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts`
- `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts`

## Dependencies

- F1 (CPU and RSS instrumentation)
- F6 (lazy per-command imports)
- F7 (fast-path budget)
data.title: Verify >=60% CPU-second reduction per refresh cycle
